name: Inside a 5-inch FPV quad
heading: Inside a
5-inch FPV quad
subtitle: A freestyle quad built part by part: every wire carries what it really carries. Move the throttle and watch the current, the motor phases and the commands change. Dive off the path into the ESC, a motor or the battery.

levels.title: 5-inch FPV quad
levels.text: Battery to ESC on two 12 AWG leads, ESC to each motor on three phase wires, the flight controller above the ESC sending four DShot commands down an 8-wire cable. Camera, VTX and receiver hang off the FC's pads.
levels.caption: Over 100 A flat out, from a pack you hold in one hand.

levels.title: SpeedyBee F405 V5 flight controller
levels.text: A 39 mm square board weighing 8.1 g. The ICM42688P gyro reports rotation thousands of times a second; the STM32F405 turns each reading into four new motor commands for the ESC.
levels.caption: Sense, decide, command: thousands of times a second.

levels.title: STM32F405 microcontroller
levels.text: A 10 × 10 mm LQFP64 package with 64 leads at 0.5 mm pitch. Inside, a 90 nm die carries a 168 MHz Cortex-M4F core, 1 MB of flash and 192 KB of RAM.
levels.caption: The whole flight runs through 64 pins.

finale.title: 64 pins fly the quad.
finale.text: Every stick input, gyro sample and motor command passes through this 10 mm chip, and every amp the motors pull is switched by the ESC below it.
